scope: Proposition 3.4 (Indexed characteristic coefficients) of the manuscript “Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy” (preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/etr-counting-hierarchy.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 141 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 151fe6144a42154d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider fixed families r1, . . . , rn, v ∈ Z[x], indexed by a word of length N. Suppose that n ≥ 1 is polynomially bounded and polynomial-time computable, that ℓ ≥ 2 and Ω ≥ 0 are short polynomial-time computable integers, and that degx ri < ℓ and degx v ≤ Ω. Put fi = xℓ i − ri, J = det(∂jfi), D = ℓn , L0 = DΩ + n(ℓ − 1). For a ≥ 0, suppose that v, the indexed ri, and J can be evaluated uniformly in Fa over prime fields with p > n(ℓ − 1) + ℓL0 + D2 + 10. (3.11) Additional short, polynomial-time computable lower cutoffs on p are allowed. Then, for every 0 ≤ d ≤ D, [yd ] det(yI − Mv) (mod p) is uniformly computable in Fa+8 in this prime range. All running-time and query-length bounds are polynomial in the length of the input, including p and the coefficient index d.
